summary: M0 model-only verdict: BENIGN @ 1.00. All signals are explained by a consistent, long-running remote-access pattern: the same device (dev-ng-01) in the same city (Manisa) authenticates from the university network (193.140.10.52 / AS-AEGEAN-EDU) during business hours with no MFA, and from a residential ISP (198.51.100.15 / AS9121 TTNET) in the evenings with MFA approved (mfa_prompt_count=1) every time. This has been stable since at least mid-September, so it is not new access, impossible travel, or a new device. The phish_suspect mail was only a delivery from a lookalike domain (aegean-edu.com.tr) with no evidence the user clicked or that credentials were entered, and the OWA inbox rule (move to Arşiv-2026) is a normal archiving action, not external forwarding or deletion. No confirmed account takeover indicators (no password reset, no new device/location, no MFA fatigue, no sent mail from the account). Suspicious signals are accounted for.
